issues.legal_issue: A scheme saved by a successor statute continues to operate without being reassessed for consistency with that statute unless it is modified through the prescribed procedure.
material_facts: A scheme for the administration of a religious institution was framed under an earlier statute and was confirmed, subject to minor modifications, after a challenge in court.
A later statute repealed and replaced the earlier statute and provided that schemes of this kind would be deemed to have been settled or modified under the later statute.
The later statute separately provided a procedure by which such a scheme could be modified or cancelled.
The challenge sought to test the scheme's consistency with the later statute in writ proceedings, rather than through the procedure for modifying or cancelling the scheme.
issues.conclusion: The saving provision continued the scheme as though it had been made under the later statute; it did not require the scheme to be reassessed or reframed for consistency with that statute. The scheme could be modified or cancelled through the procedure specifically provided for that purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed section 103(d) of the Madras Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951, together with section 62(3)(a). Unlike other clauses of section 103 that expressly addressed consistency with the later Act, section 103(d) contained no such condition. The court considered East End Dwellings Co. Ltd. v. Finsbury Borough Council but held that the deeming provision did not require schemes to be reassessed. A saved scheme continued to operate unless modified or cancelled under the statutory procedure.

predicates.scheme_made_under_repealed_law: A scheme was made under an earlier law before that law was repealed.
predicates.successor_law_saves_schemes: A later law provides that schemes of this kind are to be treated as made under that later law.
predicates.scheme_challenged_outside_modification_p: A party challenges the scheme's continued operation without using the process provided for modifying or cancelling it.

issues.definition: When a scheme made under an earlier law is saved by a later law and challenged outside the modification process, it continues without reassessment.

issues.legal_issue: A valid scheme made before the Constitution does not become subject to a fundamental-rights challenge merely because its implementation continues after the Constitution takes effect.
material_facts: The scheme was framed under a law that was valid when the scheme was made, and a prior court challenge to it had failed.
The scheme had not been fully implemented before the Constitution came into force.
After the Constitution came into force, an executive officer gave notice seeking to take over the institution's administration and properties under the scheme.
The challenge argued that the later implementation deprived the office-holder of property in violation of the constitutional guarantee.
The court distinguished the earlier decision in Seth Shanti Sarup v. Union of India, where the impugned deprivation rested on orders that were invalid under the laws under which they were issued.
issues.conclusion: The scheme could not be challenged under the constitutional guarantee merely because it had not been fully implemented before the Constitution and was sought to be implemented afterward; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The fundamental rights conferred by the Constitution are not retrospective in operation. The court applied Article 19(1)(f) and Article 13(1), and distinguished Seth Shanti Sarup v. Union of India because the orders there were invalid under the laws under which they purportedly had been made. A valid pre-Constitution scheme that had already effected the relevant deprivation was not made open to challenge merely by its continued operation after the Constitution came into force.

predicates.constitutional_rights_challenge_in_writ: A party brings writ proceedings claiming that implementation of a scheme violates a constitutional right.
predicates.scheme_validly_made_before_constitution: A scheme was validly made under the law in force before the Constitution took effect.
predicates.property_deprivation_effected_before_con: The scheme had already effected the relevant deprivation of property rights before the Constitution took effect.
predicates.implementation_continues_after_constitut: Implementation or enforcement of the scheme continues after the Constitution takes effect.

issues.definition: When a valid pre-Constitution scheme had already effected the relevant property deprivation and its implementation continues afterward, later implementation alone does not invalidate it in a constitutional-rights writ challenge.
